Public Portion 
 1. CPC - Bella Apartments Redevelopment Of Brightwood School - $100,000.00 (09/08/2026) 
 
Minutes: 
On September 14, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, reviewed a 
Community Preservation Act funding request to redevelop the former Brightwood Elementary 
School into affordable senior housing. The project requested $300,000, and the Community 
Preservation Committee recommended $100,000 to the City Council. 
 
The committee reviewed BELLA’s role in the development and related ethics questions. BELLA 
is wholly owned by the New North Citizens Council, with Vanessa Otero and City Clerk Gladys 
Oyola-López serving as managers. Representatives stated that neither manager receives personal 
financial gain from BELLA or the project and that approved funding would support the 
development. Members expressed different interpretations of the applicable disclosure, recusal, 
and conflict-of-interest requirements. Councilor Justin Hurst requested written guidance from the 
State Ethics Commission.
The proposed development is expected to exceed $40 million and provide affordable senior 
housing for households earning up to 60 percent of the area median income. The committee took 
no vote and planned to await additional ethics guidance before further consideration of the 
funding request. The meeting adjourned at 4:25 p.m.
